subject: history
title: Reform and the Vote Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the Chartists, the Reform Acts and the Suffragettes.
meta_desc: GCSE OCR History — 1832 Reform Act, Chartists and women's suffrage.
final_note: You learned how the franchise widened from 1832 to 1928.

concepts.def: 1832 — abolished rotten boroughs, added middle-class men
1838-48 working-class movement for the People's Charter
1867 — gave the vote to urban working-class men
1884 — extended the vote to rural workers
Pankhurst's WSPU, founded 1903 for women's vote
1928 — equal vote for all adults at 21

walkthroughs.body_html:
Before 1832 only about 3% of adults could vote. Rotten boroughs like Old Sarum returned MPs with 7 voters.

After Peterloo (1819) and unrest, the 1832 Great Reform Act abolished rotten boroughs and added middle-class men. The electorate grew from 400,000 to 650,000.

The People's Charter (1838) demanded universal male suffrage and the secret ballot.

Three petitions (1839, 1842, 1848) were rejected. But by 1918 five of the six demands were law. The 1867 Reform Act doubled the electorate; the 1884 Act tripled it again.

Emmeline Pankhurst founded the WSPU in 1903 — 'Deeds not words'.

Emily Davison died at the 1913 Derby. The 1918 Representation of the People Act gave women over 30 with property the vote. The 1928 Equal Franchise Act gave all women the vote at 21 — equal to men.

mcqs.q: When did women get the vote on equal terms with men?

numericals.q: In what year was the People's Charter drafted?

free_texts.q: Who founded the WSPU in 1903? Two words — first and surname.
free_texts.hint: Her daughters were Christabel and Sylvia.
